summary: Specifies how to use the DES encryption algorithm in cipher feedback mode with the Telnet encryption option. It is informational.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC defines DES cipher feedback mode for Telnet's encryption option. It explains how peers exchange an initial vector and start using a shared key.

questions: how does telnet des cfb64 start
what is a cfb64 initial vector
does telnet des cfb64 ensure integrity
subtitle: Command and key-handling rules for DES cipher feedback in Telnet encryption.

tldr.problem: This RFC specifies how the Telnet encryption option uses DES in 64-bit cipher feedback mode.
tldr.mechanism: The peers exchange an 8-byte initial vector, accept or reject it, negotiate a key identifier, and then apply DES_CFB64 to data.
tldr.outcome: The memo describes encryption behavior and notes that CFB does not ensure data integrity.

today: RFC 2952 is an Informational memo specifying a Telnet encryption option. The unit metadata lists no later update or replacement.

sections.title: The Initial Vector Commands
sections.content:
The encryption type is DES_CFB64. The sender that has negotiated WILL ENCRYPT generates a random 8-byte initial vector and sends it in a CFB64_IV command in clear text.

The peer that has DO ENCRYPT responds with CFB64_IV_OK or CFB64_IV_BAD. The RFC requires the OK response for backward compatibility; BAD is for a protocol violation such as a vector of the wrong length.
sections.plainLanguage: One side sends an 8-byte starting value before encrypted data begins. The other side replies that it accepts or rejects that value.

sections.title: Starting and Maintaining Encryption
sections.content:
After receiving CFB64_IV_OK, the encrypting side negotiates a key identifier with ENC_KEYID. Once both sides identify a common key, START and END commands can control encrypted data.

The RFC specifies when the encryption or decryption state is reinitialized after a changed key identifier or a new initial vector. It also describes how a default key from Telnet authentication is used, including limits based on key length.
sections.plainLanguage: After agreeing on the starting value, the peers select a shared key identifier. They use the selected key and vector to initialize the encryption state.

sections.title: Integrity Limitations
sections.content:
Cipher Feedback encryption does not ensure data integrity. The RFC says an active attacker who can predict plaintext has a limited ability to modify text, though changes affect blocks in a way that may make detection likely.

The memo discusses the trade-off of adding a message authentication code: it would add bytes for each character, affecting performance on slow links.
sections.plainLanguage: Encryption hides content but does not prove that no one changed it. The RFC discusses extra authentication data as a protection with added transmission cost.
